attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: Term-cover randomness does not imply a cap bound for arbitrary one-sided semantic predicates. The missing theorem is a one-sided conditional pseudorandomness statement for the distribution of generated formulas inside positive bags.
steps: Instantiate F_{N,j}(x) as polylog-length k-CNF formulas with v=beta log N variables and density near the satisfiability threshold; set Q=N^q with q in ((1+epsilon)/2,1+epsilon).
Try to upper-bound A_N(s) by first bounding hit probability of assignment or partial-term predicates under mu_N^+.
Attempt a union bound over all size-s L-input circuits P, using the hope that any large accepted set contains generated unsatisfiable formulas and hence violates one-sided soundness.
The count of circuits is 2^{O(s log s)}, and for s=N^alpha this is far too large for term-cover estimates over individual witnesses.
More seriously, one-sided soundness is semantic on the generated range: a circuit may recognize a correlated satisfiable slice with no small witness-term description.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The derivation controls explicit witness tests but not all small circuits whose accepted language is contained in SAT on the generated range. A valid proof must rule out these semantic separators or exhibit one as a falsifier.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Cycle 42: distributional cap certificate for one-sided semantic separators

assumptions: epsilon>0 is fixed and independent of N.
q and rho are constants satisfying q>(1+epsilon)/2 and max{q,rho}<1+epsilon.
The generator outputs Q formulas of length L with total charged implementation size N^{rho+o(1)}.
mu_N^+ is supported on positive bags and every exceptional set of at most E positives has mu_N^+-mass at most beta_N(E).
Local predicate size s is charged nonuniformly; the lemma does not assume uniform construction of the predicates.
definitions: source object: H_N(x)=OR_{j<=Q} SAT(F_{N,j}(x)) on N-bit inputs, with Q=N^q, L=(log N)^d, d>1, and all F_{N,j} generated by a circuit G_N of size N^{rho+o(1)}.
target object: SAT notin P/poly obtained only by contrapositive substitution from polynomial-size SAT circuits into the generated-OR carrier; this is route-level progress, not a proof of P != NP.
controlled interface: local L-bit predicates P_{j,r} of circuit size at most s, composed as P_{j,r}(F_{N,j}(x)), plus equality patching for E missed positive N-bit inputs at cost O(EN).
target-preserving condition: max{q,rho}<1+epsilon, q>(1+epsilon)/2, L=(log N)^d with d>1, and no advice leakage other than the charged nonuniform local predicates and patching equalities.
source lower-bound model: nonuniform fan-in two Boolean circuits for H_N, with the desired source claim C(H_N)>N^{1+epsilon-o(1)}.
one-sided soundness: P_{j,r}(F_{N,j}(x))=1 is forbidden for every negative bag x with H_N(x)=0; the predicate need only be sound on the actual generated range.
separator measure: Sep_N^{1s}(E;s) is the minimum K(s+L^{O(1)})+EN over K size-s local predicates that hit all but E positive inputs and have no false positives on negative inputs.
distributional cap: for a distribution mu_N^+ on H_N^{-1}(1), A_N(s)=max_{j,P} Pr_{x~mu_N^+}[P(F_{N,j}(x))=1], where P ranges over size-s one-sided predicates.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The missing bridge is a nontrivial compiler from arbitrary polynomial-size Boolean circuits to representations of degree below m. Easy max-degree P functions falsify such a compiler for the standard degree measures.
steps: Define the route measure mu and the target envelope B_{mu,T}(m,k).
The transfer implication is immediate: if SAT_m had a T-circuit C, then mu(SAT_m)=mu(C)<=B_{mu,T}(m,k), contradicting the source lower bound.
For every total m-bit Boolean function, exact degree, sign degree, and bounded-error approximate degree are at most m by exact multilinear representation.

The upper bound is tight inside unrestricted polynomial-size circuits: AND_m has exact degree m over every field, and PARITY_m has sign degree and approximate degree m while having O(m)-size Boolean circuits.
Therefore B_{mu,SIZE}(m,k)=m for k>=1, so a degree-only proof would need mu(SAT_m)>m, impossible for a total m-bit function.
For padded SAT with m=n^beta, the measured degree is at most the core length n=m^{1/beta} when the padding bits are ignored, so padding worsens the threshold rather than preserving it.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This proves a route-level obstruction only. It does not rule out SAT circuit lower bounds using information beyond degree, and it gives no evidence by itself for P != NP.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Barrier-Aware Lower-Bound Route: polynomial-degree target gate

assumptions: SAT_m is totalized on all m-bit encodings, with malformed encodings rejected.
The lower-bound proof uses only the numerical measure mu, not SAT-specific nonblack-box syntax.
The target class is unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuits, not AC0, formulas, branching programs, or algebraic circuits.
k >= 1, so SIZE(m^k) contains linear-size AND and parity implementations.
definitions: source object: a lower bound on a Boolean-function representation measure mu, with mu in {exact multilinear degree over F, sign degree over R, bounded-error approximate degree over R}, evaluated on SAT_m or a polynomially padded SAT slice.
target object: nonuniform unrestricted Boolean circuits SIZE(m^k) on the same m input bits, with fan-in two AND/OR/NOT gates and constants.
controlled interface: a target-envelope compiler B_{mu,T}(m,k) proving mu(C) <= B_{mu,T}(m,k) for every target circuit C, without changing the slice or adding advice.
target-preserving condition: the source lower bound is useful only if mu(SAT_m) > B_{mu,T}(m,k); for P vs NP this must hold for T = SIZE(m^k) for every fixed k.

attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The derivation is a complete no-go for low-ANF-degree universal predicates, but it does not construct the needed high-degree non-natural invariant and it does not eliminate existential hard-row sources with an independent selector.
steps: Represent the claimed universal invariant A_m as its reduced ANF over the N=2^m truth-table coordinates.
Let S be a maximum-size monomial with coefficient a_S=1, so |S|=K_m.
Use Mobius inversion on the subcube supported by S: a_S=\oplus_{U\subseteq S} A_m(1_U).
Since a_S=1, at least one U subset S has A_m(1_U)=1.
The accepted table 1_U has support at most K_m and therefore unrestricted circuit size O(K_m m).
If K_m m^{O(1)}<2^{epsilon m}, this accepted table is below the MCSP no-side threshold, contradicting universal soundness.
For a conjunction of T equations of degree at most d, the exact acceptance indicator is the product of the equation indicators and has ANF degree at most dT.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is route-level progress only. It falsifies a class of MCSP carrier sources; it does not prove P != NP or even produce an E lower bound without a valid hard-row source.

assumptions: A_m is not identically zero on the Boolean cube.

Circuit size is unrestricted nonuniform Boolean circuit size on m input bits.

For the fiber corollary, A_b(x)=1 exactly when all equations p_i(x)=b_i hold over F_2.
definitions: source object: a uniform Boolean acceptance predicate A_m on N=2^m truth-table bits, or a fiber p_i(x)=b_i, whose accepted tables are claimed MCSP no-side rows.
target object: an MCSP no-side carrier at threshold s(m)=2^{epsilon m} feeding the existing E lower-bound extraction with losses kappa and distinct-image entropy D.
controlled interface: E-uniform canonical enumeration of accepted images, no nonuniform length selector, and unrestricted circuit size used for MCSP soundness.

ANF degree K_m is the degree of A_m in F_2[x_1,...,x_N]/(x_i^2-x_i).
A t-sparse truth table has unrestricted circuit size O(tm) by hardwiring its support and OR-ing equality tests.

candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Source-side falsifier for low-degree nonlinear global invariants; it preserves the already valid carrier-to-E bridge but narrows admissible sources to high-ANF-degree or independently selected hard rows.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Low-ANF-degree global invariants cannot be universal MCSP no-side certificates. If a nonempty acceptance predicate A_m on N=2^m truth-table bits has Boolean ANF degree K_m, then it accepts some table of Hamming weight at most K_m, hence a table with unrestricted circuit size O(K_m m). Thus any universal source claiming MCSP threshold 2^{epsilon m} is invalid when K_m m^{O(1)}<2^{epsilon m}. For algebraic fibers p_i(x)=b_i of degree at most d, K_m<=dT, so low-degree nonlinear syndromes fail just as affine syndromes did.

dependency_updates.description: Explicit source proposals now require an ANF-degree audit of the acceptance indicator, not only E-time verification and sparsity.
Low-degree nonlinear algebraic fibers are invalid universal carriers because they contain sparse easy accepted tables.
The carrier-to-E transfer with delta<epsilon/(kappa(1+D)) remains valid after an actual hard row is certified.
Find a bounded-D, cap-compatible, advice-free invariant with ANF degree at least the MCSP threshold or with independent hard-row recovery.

falsifiers: Low-ANF-degree acceptance K_m<2^{epsilon m}/poly(m) is a concrete falsifier for universal MCSP no-side soundness.
Quadratic, cubic, or bounded-degree polynomial fibers with dT below the MCSP threshold are contaminated by sparse easy tables.
Affine syndrome sources remain falsified as the degree-1 special case.
A high-degree invariant implemented through subthreshold random access is invalid by leakage even if the ANF audit passes.
A nonuniform length selector or advice-dependent hard-row choice invalidates the target-preserving E extraction.
Existential hard rows inside a contaminated set do not help unless multiplexing or a uniform hard-row recovery certificate is supplied.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: When beta<epsilon-o(1), every nonempty fiber contains an accepted table of support at most 2^{beta m+1}, hence circuit size below 2^{epsilon m}; the source is invalid. Only beta>=epsilon-o(1), or an independent hard-row selector, can survive the falsifier.
held_fixed_controls: Unrestricted circuit size is the MCSP target model.
No advice or nonuniform length selector is allowed.
Canonical enumeration and padding remain E-uniform.
The claimed no-side threshold epsilon and extraction losses kappa,D are held fixed.
gedanken_experiment_design.need_decision: use now as a falsifier probe
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch needs to decide whether nonlinear global invariants repair the affine no-go. The ANF-degree experiment gives a quantitative threshold instead of another abstract barrier citation.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: For each m, let N=2^m and define a candidate MCSP carrier as the nonempty fiber of T=2^{beta m} quadratic equations over F_2 in the N truth-table bits, with kappa=1, D=0, and claimed threshold s(m)=2^{epsilon m}.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: Before intuition may enter the proof queue, the source must certify ANF degree at least 2^{epsilon m-o(m)} or certify a selected hard row, while preserving no-advice E-uniformity and avoiding subthreshold ranked random access.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: beta, the exponent controlling total ANF degree K<=2T=2^{beta m+1}.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 42 proves a new source-side no-go: any nonempty low-ANF-degree acceptance predicate over truth-table bits accepts a sparse table, so it cannot universally certify MCSP hardness above its ANF degree times equality-test overhead. This extends the affine-syndrome falsifier to bounded-degree nonlinear fibers and identifies high ANF degree, not mere nonlinearity, as the next required invariant.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Audit candidate high-degree global invariants, starting with determinant/permanent-like algebraic predicates on reshaped truth tables, for ANF degree, accepted-image entropy D, verifier cap alpha_V, and absence of ranked random-access leakage.

cycle_learning: This research cycle converted active route pressure into typed branch lemmas. The main mathematical change is that each branch now names a source object, target object, equation, validity condition, falsifier, and next experiment. Only research-mode cycles with elapsed-time and branch-engine evidence count as genuine long-horizon research progress.
